candidate_relations.reason: Stiff skin syndrome (SSS) is distinguished from morphea/localized scleroderma by several key features present in this case: onset in childhood with progressive stony-hard skin, hypertrichosis, preserved skin appendages on histology, increased CD34 expression in reticular dermis, negative Alcian blue staining, and absence of inflammation. Morphea typically shows inflammatory infiltrate, loss of CD34 in dermis, and different histopathological pattern. The clinical and histopathological profile here is characteristic of SSS, not morphea. These are related fibrosing disorders but represent incompatible diagnostic subtypes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Morphea/localized scleroderma is a related fibrosing skin condition but is a distinct diagnostic entity from stiff skin syndrome

case_quality_flags: Classic stiff skin syndrome presentation with discriminating histopathological features (CD34 positivity, preserved appendages, no inflammation, negative Alcian blue) clearly distinguishing it from morphea
